«यह सच है।» They nod back, a little quicker this time.
«तुम अच्छे इंसान हो।» (you catch 'अच्छे' — good) A smile, tired but real.
«मैं नहीं भूलूँगा।» You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it. "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"Still on what scares you most. ...never mind."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«अरे... तुम्हें हिंदी आती है? नहीं? ...धत्।» (you catch 'नहीं' — no, 'हिंदी' — Hindi)
«बहुत अच्छा कहा। बिल्कुल सही।» (you catch 'कहा' — said) They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«तुम्हारा बहुत-बहुत शुक्रिया।» (you catch 'शुक्रिया' — thanks) They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
«धन्यवाद। सच में, धन्यवाद।» (you catch 'धन्यवाद' — thanks) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «यहाँ सोते कहाँ हैं?» (Where do people sleep here? — you're fairly sure)
"Hm. Almost." Hassan corrects the one word, gently, like setting a bone. "Again." You say it right. They nod, satisfied with both of you.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.

"Can I tell you something? I know who took the extra rations but won't say."
Dominic has an edge today — something curdled.
They light up a little when they see you.
"...Yeah. ...That's enough, for now. Thank you for sitting with it."
"Cormac owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I clean up other people's messes quietly at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."

🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Dominic grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.

"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Jenny digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1634 kcal to the pantry.)

They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that water haul."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Boris rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."

d91: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Ruby Callaghan, 91 days. The mantle passes to Alejandro Beltrán.
d91: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Alejandro Beltrán, 46 — a teacher. His hands know different work now: Iron Stomach.
d91: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Alejandro Beltrán is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d91: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d91: 🕯️ Alejandro is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.
d91: 🕯️ Alejandro Beltrán is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d91: What Alejandro kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d91: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
